One status delta versus prior runs' stored logs was investigated and ruled out as not caused by this change: prctl02 shows 'skip' here where run-iIbwju's and run-atDPcd's logs had it passing. Three checks cleared it. (1) Scope: the patch touches only kernel/src/syscall/timerfd_gettime.rs and all.txt; a grep of the diff for prctl, seccomp, thp and capability returns zero hits, and the change is a pure deletion of a null-pointer guard inside one 36-line syscall handler. (2) Isolated selector boot on the fixed kernel with CONFORMANCE_TEST_SELECTOR=prctl02,timerfd_gettime01: prctl02 skip, timerfd_gettime01 pass, 16 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 5 skipped, make exit 0. (3) Most conclusively, I stashed the kernel half of the patch (git checkout of timerfd_gettime.rs, guard confirmed restored at line 17) and re-ran the same selector at this run's own base commit e8f2b9ca6 with only the all.txt edit in place: prctl02 skipped there too, identically, while timerfd_gettime01 failed (15 passed / 1 failed / 0 broken / 5 skipped, make exit 2). So prctl02's skip is independent of this patch and the sole behavioural difference the patch makes is timerfd_gettime01 fail -> pass. This matches run-iIbwju's recorded finding that prctl02's TCONF branches are probe-driven (setup() probes PR_GET_SECCOMP, PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, PR_GET_THP_DISABLE, PR_CAP_AMBIENT, PR_GET_SPECULATION_CTRL and marks each unsupported on EINVAL), a plausible source of run-to-run variation. After restoring the fix I confirmed the working diff is byte-identical to fix.json's patch.diff apart from git index lines.

That stashed run also serves as this round's baseline confirmation: it reproduces diagnose.json's failure precisely, so the kernel deletion is demonstrably what turns the suite green rather than the pool edit alone.
